# Cue — every day is a page

Daily notes and to-dos for Mac and iPhone. Fast, quiet and keyboard-first. Free, open
source, and no tracking.

> This file is the website’s own writing in plain text, for anyone — person or assistant —
> who would rather read it that way. The Terms and Privacy Policy are summarized here but
> not reproduced: those pages at https://www.usecue.today/terms and
> https://www.usecue.today/privacy are the only versions that count.

Site: https://www.usecue.today
Source: https://github.com/zlwaterfield/cue
Made by Zach Waterfield, Toronto, Canada. A personal project, in beta, used every day since
October 17, 2026.

---

# Home — https://www.usecue.today/

**Every day is a page.** Daily notes and to-dos for Mac and iPhone. Fast, quiet and
keyboard-first.

## Why I built it

I wanted one place to put the day. Not a project manager or a second brain, just a page for
today that I could open and type into without deciding where anything goes first.

Every tool I tried wanted a project, a tag or a priority before it would take a note. So I
built Cue, for myself: days are the only structure, the keyboard does everything, and it’s
ready before I’ve finished thinking of what to write.

## What makes it different

**The day is the only folder.** Things belong to dates, not projects. No tags, priorities or
dashboards. Whatever didn’t get done moves to tomorrow with ⌘D.

**Keyboard first.** Tab nests, ⌘↩ completes, and ⌘K does everything else, including dates
like “move to fri”. The mouse still works.

**Fast, and measured.** Ready to type 240 ms after launch, even with five years of notes. A
keystroke renders in 1.5 ms. Every number has a budget and a test.

**On your Mac and your iPhone.** Saved as you type, with no telemetry, and the Mac exports
to Markdown or JSON any time. Neither app needs an account; turn on sync and the same
notes are on both. Free, both ways.

Cue stays small on purpose: no reminders, recurring tasks, collaboration or AI in the app.

## Where it’s at

It’s in beta, and it’s free. Cue is my daily driver on my Mac and my iPhone, and it runs
without any issues. The Mac app is a free download that works offline with no account, and
the iPhone app is in beta on TestFlight.

Want the same notes on both? Sign in with Apple or your email and they sync, free as well.
That’s the only part with a server in it: a Postgres database at Supabase, and the MCP
endpoint, and nothing else. No tracking either way, and the code is open if you’d rather
build it yourself.

# Download — https://www.usecue.today/download

Free on your Mac and iPhone, with no account. Turn on sync whenever you like.

## Cue for Mac

Works offline, totally free. No account, no sign-up: open it and start typing. Apple silicon
Mac, signed and notarized. The download is 1.0.0-beta.2, a 122 MB .dmg, from
https://github.com/zlwaterfield/cue/releases

## Cue for iPhone

Today’s page in your pocket, on its own or synced with your Mac. The same core as the Mac
app, built for touch. Free, no account needed, and in beta on TestFlight:
https://testflight.apple.com/join/KyVXdDgz

## Accounts and privacy

**No account needed.** Each app is complete on its own. Your notes live on your Mac or
iPhone, and without an account nothing you write ever leaves it.

**An account for sync.** To have the same notes on your Mac and iPhone, turn on sync on both
and sign in with Apple or your email. The notes already on each one come along.

**No tracking.** Cue doesn’t know how you use it: nothing in either app reports back. Your
notes are only ever used to sync them between your devices, and nothing about you is sold.

**Yours to take, or delete.** Export everything from the Mac, as Markdown or JSON, any
time. Turning sync off keeps every note on your Mac or iPhone, and deleting your account
in Settings deletes it from the server.

Cue is open source, so you can read exactly what it does, build it yourself or run your own
sync server. It’s all on GitHub: https://github.com/zlwaterfield/cue

---

# Assistants — https://www.usecue.today/assistants

**There’s no AI in Cue. There’s a door.** Cue will never write your notes for you, suggest a
to-do or summarize your week. Instead it speaks MCP, the protocol assistants use to reach
tools, so the assistant you already talk to can work on your days the way another device
would. An edit it makes goes through the same sync everything else does and shows up on your
Mac and iPhone about a second later. It’s free, like the rest of Cue.

Connecting one:

1. Turn on sync in Cue’s Settings, on the Mac or the iPhone. An assistant works with your
   account rather than your computer, so this is the one part that needs one.
2. Add a custom connector in Claude, ChatGPT or whatever you use, with the URL
   https://www.usecue.today/mcp (keep the www).
3. Sign in and press Allow. The assistant sends you to Cue’s own consent page, which signs you
   in with a six-digit code by email and asks whether to connect.

Disconnect any assistant, any time, at https://www.usecue.today/oauth/consent

The five tools: `get_day` returns one day’s page, in order, nested, as Markdown.
`find_todos` returns to-dos across up to a year of days, the open ones unless it asks for
more. `search` returns lines containing every word, newest days first. `add_lines` adds
Markdown lines at the end of a day or after a particular line. `update_lines` checks off or
reopens, changes a line’s type, rewrites its text, or moves lines — with whatever is nested
under them — to another day.

**Nothing deletes.** There is no tool for it, and the database refuses it too: a token an
assistant holds can’t delete a line or the account even if it asks Supabase directly, can’t
set a password on the account, and can’t change its email address on its own. Every read and
write runs as you under Postgres row-level security, and the database checks the token’s
signature on every query.

Technically it is one Supabase Edge Function acting as another sync client: no extra server,
no new table, no service key. The details are in
https://github.com/zlwaterfield/cue/blob/main/docs/MCP.md

---

# Questions people ask

**Is Cue really free?** Yes. There’s no paid plan, no trial, no credit card and no upsell.
Sync is free too. It’s a personal project, not a business, and I don’t plan to charge for it.

**Is it open source?** Yes, MIT licensed, the whole thing: the Mac app, the iPhone app, the
sync server and this website. https://github.com/zlwaterfield/cue

**Does it work offline?** Completely. Both apps keep your notes on the device and need no
network at all. Without sync, the only thing the Mac app does online is ask GitHub, every few
hours, whether there's a newer version of Cue.

**Where are my notes stored?** On the Mac, in one SQLite file at
`~/Library/Application Support/Cue/cue.sqlite`, with a daily snapshot kept for 14 days. On
the iPhone, in the app’s own SQLite database. With sync on, also in a Postgres database at
Supabase.

**Do I need an account?** Only to sync between devices. Both apps work fully without one.

**Does Cue track me?** No. No analytics, no telemetry, no crash reporting, no ads, and no
cookies on this website. Nothing is sold or shared.

**Do you train AI on my notes?** No, never. Your notes are only used to sync them back to
your own devices.

**Can I use Cue with Claude or ChatGPT?** Yes, over MCP, if sync is on. The assistant can read
your days, add to-dos, check them off and move them, and what it does syncs to your devices
like any other edit. It can’t delete anything. There is still no AI inside the app itself.

**What servers does Cue use?** With sync off, none of Cue's: the Mac app only asks GitHub,
every few hours, whether there's a newer version. With it on, two: a Postgres database
at Supabase that holds your notes, where row-level security means an account can only ever read
its own rows, and the MCP endpoint an assistant talks to. There is nothing else — no analytics
service, no ad network, no third party.

**How fast is it?** Ready to type 240 ms after launch with five years of notes (36,543
items). A keystroke to a rendered frame is 1.5 ms, p95 3.7 ms. Searching all 36,543 items
takes 0.5 ms. Every number is checked against a budget by `pnpm bench`, on the real packaged
app.

**What doesn’t it do?** No projects, tags, priorities, folders, reminders, recurring tasks,
attachments, collaboration, dashboards or AI writing your notes. That’s on purpose.

**What are the shortcuts?** ⌘K command palette, ⌘F search, ⌘1/⌘2/⌘3 today/tomorrow/this
week, ⌘[ and ⌘] previous and next day, ⌘J go to date, ⌘N new item, ⌘↩ complete, ⇧⌘↩ toggle
bullet and to-do, Tab and ⇧Tab indent and outdent, ⌥↑ and ⌥↓ move, ⌘D move to tomorrow,
⇧⌘D move to a date, ⌘Z undo, and ⌘/ for the whole list.

# Terms of Service — https://www.usecue.today/terms

In short: Cue is free, in beta, and provided as it is. What you write belongs to you. Don’t
misuse the service or other people’s accounts. You can export your notes and delete your
account at any time.

The full text is at https://www.usecue.today/terms — that page is the version that counts.

# Privacy Policy — https://www.usecue.today/privacy

In short: your notes are yours, and they’re used only to sync them to your devices. No ads,
analytics, tracking pixels or third-party trackers, in the apps or on this site. No AI: Cue
never sends your notes to an AI model or uses them to train one. Without sync, nothing you
write leaves your device.

The full text is at https://www.usecue.today/privacy — that page is the version that counts.
